section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability
section_1.content: Define conditional probability P(A|B) as the 're-weighted' probability of A given that B has occurred. Use a Venn Diagram animation where the sample space shrinks from the whole box to just circle B.
section_1.example: Visualizing a grid of 100 people: 50 play sports, 20 are athletes. P(Athlete | Sports) focuses only on the 50 sports players.

section_2.title: The Concept of Independence
section_2.content: Define independence: Events A and B are independent if P(A|B) = P(A). Explain this as 'knowing B tells you nothing new about A'. Visualize this with two separate, non-overlapping probability trees.
section_2.example: Flipping a coin twice: The result of the first flip does not change the odds of the second flip being heads.

section_3.title: Introduction to Bayes' Theorem
section_3.content: Introduce the formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Frame this as 'Updating Beliefs'. Use an animation showing a Prior probability evolving into a Posterior probability through the lens of new evidence B.
section_3.example: A diagnostic test for a rare disease: P(Disease | Positive Test) is often counter-intuitive because P(Disease) is very low (the Prior).

section_4.title: Bayes and Independence: The Critical Link
section_4.content: Discuss how independence simplifies Bayes' Theorem. If A and B are independent, P(A|B) = P(A), making the evidence useless. Show a mathematical collapse of the formula to demonstrate why independence is the 'zero-information' state.
section_4.example: If a weather report is independent of actual rainfall, the Bayes calculation shows the report provides zero update to the probability of rain.

section_5.title: Application: The Detective Case
section_5.content: Synthesize the knowledge. A detective uses Bayes to update the probability that a suspect is guilty based on a piece of evidence. Contrast the 'Independent' case (evidence is noise) vs. the 'Dependent' case (evidence provides information).
section_5.example: A cat-detective (Detective Whiskers) evaluating if a suspect stole the fish: The evidence 'footprint size' is dependent on the suspect's height, allowing for a Bayesian update.
